finding: Existing recorded source findings preserved, no external rights re-investigation or upgrade. Currey1912 and Kurz1893 are retrospective sources for first fort1803–1812.

sources.citation: 'Bird’s-Eye View of Old Fort Dearborn.' Illustration at p. 27 of J. Seymour Currey, The Story of Old Fort Dearborn (Chicago: A. C. McClurg & Co., 1912). Numbered reconstruction of the first fort, not a contemporary view.
sources.author: Illustrator uncredited in the consulted caption; J. Seymour Currey is the book author
sources.describes_date: the first Fort Dearborn, 1803–1812, reconstructed retrospectively

sources.citation: Kurz & Allison. Chicago In Early Days, 1779-1857. Chicago: Kurz & Allison, 76 & 78 Wabash Avenue, 1893. Chromolithograph, fifteen numbered vignettes with printed key.
sources.author: Kurz & Allison

sources.rights_note: The sheet carries its own copyright line at the foot, read off the committed copy verbatim: "Copyrighted 1893 by Kurz & Allison, 76 & 78 Wabash Avenue, Chicago, Ills." A US copyright first secured in 1893 has expired, which is why this record is public_domain rather than check_required, and it is the only plate in this project's pictorial set whose rights are settled ON THE OBJECT rather than by inference. The Library of Congress copy at the url carries no restriction of its own.
